question: What does a genitourinary neoplasm involve?

options.A: Inflammation of the prostate gland caused by pathogens
options.B: Chronic bacterial infections of the lower urinary tract
options.C: Abnormal tissue growths in the urinary and male reproductive systems
options.D: Sudden loss of kidney filtration due to dehydration

explanation: Think of a neoplasm simply as an abnormal growth or tumor. When we say genitourinary, we mean the organs of the urinary system and the male reproductive tract. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why is early recognition of genitourinary growths so important?

options.A: It directly improves survival rates and quality of life
options.B: It guarantees that the tumor will remain completely benign
options.C: It completely prevents the need for any future blood tests
options.D: It ensures the patient will never require surgical intervention

explanation: Catching these growths early gives our patients the best fighting chance. Prompt care stops things from getting worse and helps keep them comfortable and healthy. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h1)

question: What is the main trigger for cancer starting in the body?

options.A: Genetic mutations that cause uncontrolled cell division
options.B: Overgrowth of normal flora inside the renal pelvis
options.C: A sudden decrease in daily fluid intake and hydration
options.D: Temporary blockages in the main ureter passageways

explanation: Cancer begins when changes happen in cellular DNA. Normally, cells grow and die in an orderly way, but mutations tell them to keep dividing without stopping. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h2)

question: Why does cigarette smoking strongly increase the risk of bladder cancer?

options.A: Tobacco smoke reduces blood flow to the external genitalia
options.B: Carcinogens from tobacco are filtered by the kidneys and sit in the bladder
options.C: Nicotine directly damages the muscular layers of the ureters
options.D: Smoking completely stops the bladder walls from expanding properly

explanation: When someone smokes, the toxic chemicals enter their bloodstream. The kidneys filter these out into the urine, where they sit in the bladder and irritate the lining over time. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h2)

question: What is a key difference between benign and malignant tumors?

options.A: Malignant tumors stay completely contained within a capsule
options.B: Malignant tumors never grow back after simple removal
options.C: Benign tumors do not spread to distant parts of the body
options.D: Benign tumors always require immediate chemotherapy

explanation: A great way to remember this in the wards is that benign tumors stay put and grow slowly. Malignant tumors are the ones that can invade other tissues and spread around. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h3)

question: Why must a nurse remember that not every large or palpable mass in the genitourinary area is cancer?

options.A: Non-cancerous conditions like BPH can also create large, feelable masses
options.B: Malignant tumors are impossible to feel during a physical exam
options.C: Palpable masses are only ever caused by trapped fluid pockets
options.D: Benign growths always shrink on their own without any treatment

explanation: Conditions like benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) can make an organ swell up big enough to feel during an exam, which is why doctors always order tests like biopsies to be sure. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h3)

question: Which symptom is a major warning sign for bladder cancer?

options.B: Painful swelling of the knee joints

explanation: Gross hematuria means blood in the urine that you can actually see with the naked eye. When it comes on without any pain, it's a classic red flag for the bladder. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h4)

question: A 25-year-old male client reports finding a hard, painless lump in his left testicle. What should the nurse suspect first?
explanation: Testicular cancer is most commonly seen in young adult men. A painless lump or swelling in the scrotum should always be checked out right away. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a cystoscopy for suspected bladder cancer?

options.A: To directly view the bladder lining and take tissue samples
options.B: To measure the exact filtration rate of both kidneys
options.C: To flush out bacterial infections from the lower ureters
options.D: To check the blood level of prostate-specific antigen

explanation: A cystoscopy uses a thin, lighted tube passed through the urethra. It lets the doctor look right inside the bladder and grab a small tissue sample if something looks unusual. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h5)

question: Why can early diagnosis of genitourinary cancers sometimes be delayed?

options.A: Blood tests usually show completely normal results for years
options.B: Patients refuse to provide urine samples during routine visits
options.C: Tumors in these organs never cause any noticeable signs
options.D: Their early symptoms often mimic common urinary tract infections

explanation: Symptoms like burning when you pee or seeing a little blood can easily be mistaken for a simple UTI, which is why sometimes treatment gets delayed while trying antibiotics first. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h5)

question: What does a radical prostatectomy involve?

options.A: Radiation treatment applied only to the renal pelvis
options.B: Surgical removal of the entire prostate gland
options.C: Chemical blockage of male hormones in the testes
options.D: Destruction of bladder stones using laser energy

explanation: When a patient has localized prostate cancer, a radical prostatectomy is done to take out the whole prostate gland and some nearby tissues to get the cancer out. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h6)

question: Why is hormone therapy often used to treat prostate cancer?

options.A: It replaces the need for surgical removal of the bladder
options.B: Prostate cancer growth is often fueled by male sex hormones
options.C: Hormone drugs permanently cure all forms of kidney tumors
options.D: It stops the kidneys from producing excess red blood cells

explanation: Many prostate cancer cells need testosterone to grow and thrive. By lowering these hormone levels in the body, we can help slow down or shrink the tumor. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h6)

question: A client returns to the ward after having a TURBT (transurethral resection of a bladder tumor). What is your priority nursing check?

options.A: Assessing for bilateral swelling of the lower leg joints
options.B: Checking for sudden changes in visual acuity and hearing
options.C: Monitoring urinary output and watching for bleeding
options.D: Measuring fasting blood glucose levels every two hours

explanation: After bladder surgery, keeping a close eye on their urine through the catheter is vital. We watch for bright red blood or clots so we can catch any bleeding early! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h7)

question: Why should nurses be ready to talk about body image and sexual health with GU cancer patients?

options.A: Surgeries and treatments in this area directly affect elimination and sexual health
options.B: Talking about these topics completely eliminates the need for pain medication
options.C: Incontinence and sexual changes only occur in elderly female clients
options.D: Psychological support speeds up the physical regeneration of kidney tissue

explanation: Treatments for these cancers touch some of the most personal parts of a patient's life. Being a compassionate, open listener helps them cope with changes in how their body works. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h7)

question: What is a very common challenge for clients after prostate surgery?

options.A: Permanent loss of the ability to digest proteins
options.B: Chronic infections of the upper respiratory tract
options.D: Sudden enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck

explanation: Because the prostate sits right next to the nerves and muscles controlling urination and erections, surgery here often causes temporary or lasting trouble with both functions. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h8)

question: How do pelvic floor exercises help patients recovering from GU cancer treatments?

options.A: They increase testosterone production in the testes
options.B: They strengthen muscles to help regain bladder control
options.C: They improve the filtration rate of the renal cortex
options.D: They prevent the recurrence of cancerous cell growth

explanation: Pelvic floor exercises (like Kegels) tone up the muscles supporting the bladder and urethra, which is a huge help for clients dealing with leakage after surgery. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h8)
